html:
Peru is a country on the Pacific coast of South America, between the desert coast, the Andes and the Amazon. It declared independence in 1821.

It has one of the longest histories in the Americas: Caral, one of the oldest cities in the world, then Chavín, Moche, Nazca, Wari and Chimú, and finally the Inca Empire ruled from Cusco. After the Spanish conquest, Lima was the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru. José de San Martín declared independence in 1821, and the Battle of Ayacucho in 1824 ended Spanish rule in South America.

In the years shown on the map from 1880:

  • The guano boom, selling bird droppings as fertiliser, had made the state rich and then left it in debt.
  • In the War of the Pacific Chile occupied Lima in 1881 and took the southern nitrate provinces.
  • A small elite ran the country in the early 1900s, while new parties such as APRA spoke for workers and Native people.
  • A left-wing military government from 1968 broke up the great estates.

From 1980 the Maoist Shining Path waged a war that killed tens of thousands, most of them poor Andean villagers. Alberto Fujimori, elected in 1990, defeated it but shut down Congress in 1992 and was later jailed for abuses. The Inca city of Machu Picchu, brought to world attention in 1911, is now Peru's best-known site.
sum: Peru is a country on the Pacific coast of South America, between the desert coast, the Andes and the Amazon. It declared independence in 1821.
